Will it happen today? After dining, will the supreme lord grant an audience at his station, or will he come out to the outer enclosure?'—spending the day in hope of an audience—surrounded on all sides by the great feudatory kings conquered by his arms; and attended by other great sovereigns from various lands who had come through either fear or affection, awaiting the time for the king's audience; and attended by <s>Jainas</s>, <s>Ārhat</s> monks, <s>Pāśupatas</s>, followers of <s>Pārāśari</s>, and mendicants, seated apart, and by people born in every country, and by barbarian tribes dwelling on every ocean-shore-forest-belt, and by delegations of envoys arrived from every land—as if it were the creation-ground of all subjects belonging to the

children.text: prajā-patīnāṃ, loka-traya-sārôccaya-racitaṃ caturtham iva lokam, mahā-bhārata-śatair apy a-kathanīya-samṛddhi-saṃbhāram, kṛta-yuga-sahasrair iva kalpita-saṃniveśam, svargârbudair iva vihita-rāmaṇīyakam, rāja-lakṣmī-koṭibhir iva kṛta-parigrahaṃ rāja-dvāram agamat.
children.translated_text: <s>Prajāpatis</s>, a fourth world as it were, fashioned from the accumulated essence of the three worlds, a store of prosperity indescribable even by hundreds of <s>Mahābhāratas</s>, an establishment as if arranged over thousands of <s>Kṛta</s> ages, of a loveliness as if contrived by billions of heavens, as if taken into possession by tens of millions of royal fortunes—he reached the royal gate.

body.translated_text: On the first day, slowly passing through the grove of the <s>Caṇḍikā</s> temple—distressing with the heat of summer, waterless, rough with leafless trees, with <s>Kātyāyanī</s> shrines carved on the entrance-trees worshipped by travelers, though dry yet appearing to sprout with the thousands of dangling restless tongue-creepers of thirsty wild animal herds, appearing to bristle with the bee-swarms set in motion by the honey-balls being licked by bears and langurs, appearing to have goosebumps with the hundreds of thick <s>abhīru</s> bulbs growing on the scorched ground—he went to a village named <s>Mallakūṭa</s>. There, hospitably received by his brother and friend named <s>Jagatpati</s>, who was inseparable from his heart, he rested comfortably. Then, the next day, crossing the blessed <s>Bhāgīrathī</s>, he spent the night in a forest village named <s>Yaṣṭigṛhaka</s>. On another day, he reached the encampment established near <s>Maṇipura</s> along the <s>Ajiravati</s> river. And he stayed not far from the royal quarters.

body.text: abhavac câsya jāta-vismayasya manasi: "katham ivêdam iyat-pramāṇaṃ prāṇi-jātaṃ janayatāṃ prajā-sṛjāṃ nâsīt pariśramaḥ, mahā-bhūtānāṃ vā parikṣayaḥ, paramâṇūnāṃ vā vicchedaḥ, kālasya vântaḥ, āyuṣo vā vyuparamaḥ, ākṛtīnāṃ vā parisamāptiḥ" iti. Mekhalakas tu dūrād eva dvāra-pāla-lokena pratyabhijñāyamānaḥ "tiṣṭhatu tāvat kṣaṇa-mātram atrâiva puṇya-bāgī" iti tam abhidhāyâpratihataḥ puraḥ prāviśat.
body.translated_text: And in his wonder-struck mind arose [the thought]: 'How is it that the <s>Prajāpatis</s> (creators), in generating such a vast multitude of living beings, felt no exhaustion? Or the great elements no diminution? Or the atoms no severance? Or time no end? Or lifespan no cessation? Or forms no completion?' But <s>Mekhalaka</s>, being recognized from afar by the company of gate-keepers, said to him, 'Let the blessed one stand here just for a moment,' and entered ahead without obstruction.

body.text: atha sa muhūrtād iva prāṃśunā, karṇikāra-gaureṇa, vīdhra-kañcuka-cchanna-vapuṣā, samunmiṣan-māṇikya-padaka-bandha-bandhura-vasta-bandha-kṛśâvalagnena, hima-śaila-śilā-viśāla-vakṣasā, hara-vṛṣa-kakuda-kūṭa-vikaṭâṃsa-taṭena, urasā capala-hṛṣīka-hariṇa-kula-saṃyamana-pāśam iva hāraṃ bibhratā, "kathayataṃ yadi soma-vaṃśa-saṃbhavaḥ sūrya-vaṃśa-saṃbhavo vā bhū-patir abhūd evaṃ-vidhaḥ" iti praṣṭum ānītābhyāṃ soma-sūryābhyām iva śravaṇa-gatābhyāṃ maṇi-kuṇḍalābyāṃ samudbhāsamānena, vahad-vadana-lāvaṇya-visara-veṇikâkṣipyamāṇair adhikāra-gauravād dīyamāna-mārgeṇêva dina-kṛtaḥ kiraṇaiḥ prasāda-labdhayā vikaca-puṇḍarīka-muṇḍa-mālayêva dīrghayā dṛṣṭyā dūrād evânandayatā, naiṣṭhuryâdhiṣṭhāne 'pi pratiṣṭhitena pade pade praśrayam ivâvanamreṇa,

children.text: maulinā pāṇḍuram uṣṇīṣam udvahatā, vāmena sthūla-muktā-phala-cchuraṇa-dantura-tsaruṃ kara-kisalayena kalayatā kṛpāṇam, itareṇâpanīta-taralatāṃ tāḍanīm iva latāṃ śātakaumbhīṃ vetrayaṣṭim unmṛṣṭāṃ dhārayatā puruṣeṇânugamyamāno nirgatyâvocat: "eṣa khalu mahā-pratīhārāṇām an-antaraś cakṣuṣyo devasya Pāriyātra-nāmā dauvārikaḥ. samanugṛhṇātv enam anurūpayā pratipattyā kalyāṇâbhiniveśī" iti. dauvārikas tu samupasṛtya kṛta-praṇāmo madhurayā girā sa-vinayam abhāṣata: "āgacchata. praviśata deva-darśanāya. kṛta-prasādo devaḥ" iti. Bāṇas tu "dhanyo 'smi, yad evam anugrāhyaṃ māṃ devo manyate" ity uktvā tenôpadiśyamāna-mārgaḥ prāviśad abhyantaram.
children.translated_text: wearing a white turban on his head, holding in his left hand a sword whose hilt was rough with the splendor of large pearls, grasped by his sprout-like hand, carrying in his other [hand] a golden staff—polished, like a creeper from which fickleness had been removed, like a rod of chastisement—[<s>Mekhalaka</s>] came out and said: 'This, indeed, is the chief of the great door-keepers, dear to the eyes of the lord, named <s>Pāriyātra</s>, a door-keeper without equal. May the well-disposed one favor him with appropriate courtesy.' The door-keeper, having approached and made his salutation, spoke sweetly and respectfully: 'Come. Enter for the audience with the lord. The lord has granted his favor.' And <s>Bāṇa</s>, having said, 'I am blessed, that the lord considers me worthy of such grace,' entered the inner [quarters], guided along the path indicated by him.

body.translated_text: Then, after what seemed but a moment, accompanied by a man—tall, golden as a <s>karṇikāra</s> flower, his body covered by a leather tunic, with a thin sash made beautiful by the clasp of a half-opening ruby pendant-setting, his chest broad as a slab of the snowy mountain, his shoulder-ridge massive like the hump-peak of <s>Śiva</s>'s bull, wearing on his breast a necklace as if it were the taming-noose for the herd of restless sense-deer, his face resplendent with a pair of jeweled ear-rings at his ears as if <s>Soma</s> and <s>Sūrya</s> had been brought close to ask, 'Tell—was the king who was thus born of the lunar dynasty or the solar dynasty?', gladdening [all] from afar with a long gaze like a garland of opened white lotus heads, as if a rosary bestowed by [royal] favor, through which the spreading stream of his facial charm was flowing, which parted way for him as if out of respect for his authority, [a gaze] like the rays of the sun granting passage; at every step bowing humbly even while standing in a station of severity,

children.translated_text: —with joints, with compressed chests, with hoof-discs hard as iron platforms extending in straight, not-too-thick lines, bearing round bellies as if their entrails had not been fashioned—from fear of being torn apart by excessive speed—with broad haunches divided by rising hip-bones, with tender sprout-like tails swaying upon the ground, somehow restrained by strong, abundant ropes firmly fixed on both sides, though tall, appearing yet taller with a single hind leg involuntarily stretched back by the rope-binding, with neck-bells strung on multi-stranded cords, with half-closed eyes, shaking itchy spots of quivering skin dappled with dark-green foam-flecks from <s>dūrvā</s>-grass juice released from their teeth-grip, with languidly curled tails, with one half of the haunch loosened and drooping from the fatigue of resting on a single hoof, and meditating as it were in drowsiness, and making soft, faint sounds of stumbling snorts, and desiring grass with hooves striking the ground—the earth-surface scratched by hoof-tips resounding loudly—and with agitation arisen from jealousy over the taste of scattered fodder-morsels, and with pupils rolling, trembling, and fearful from the fierce angry shouts of violent grooms, as if being guarded by the constantly present auspicious-lamp fire due to their bodies made tawny by saffron-smearing—

children.text: -pari-vitata-vitānaiḥ, puraḥ-pūjitâbhimata-daivataiḥ, bhū-pāla-vallabhais turaṅgair āracitāṃ mandurāṃ vilokayan, kutūhalâkṣipta-hṛdayaḥ kiñ-cid antaram atikrānto hasta-vāmenâty-uccatayā nir-avakāśam ivâkāśaṃ kurvāṇam, mahatā kadalī-vanena parivṛta-paryantaṃ sarvato madhu-karamayībhir mada-srutibhir nadībhir ivâpatantībhir āpūryamāṇam, āśā-mukha-visarpiṇā bakula-vanānām iva vikasatām āmodena limpantaṃ ghrāṇêndriyaṃ dūrād avyaktam ibha-dhiṣṇyâgāram apaśyat. apṛcchac ca: "atra devaḥ kiṃ karoti?" iti. asāv akathayat: "eṣa khalu devasyâupavāhyo vāhyaṃ hṛdayaṃ jāty-antarita ātmā bahiś-carāḥ prāṇā vikrama-krīḍā-suhṛd Darpaśāta iti yathârtha-nāmā vāraṇa-patiḥ. tasyâvasthāna-maṇḍapo 'yaṃ mahān dṛśyate" iti. sa tam avādīt: "bhadra! śrūyate Darpaśātaḥ. yady evam a-doṣo vā paśyāmi tāvad vāraṇêndram eva. ato 'rhasi mām atra prāpayitum. ati-paravān asmi kūtūhalena" iti. so 'bhāṣata: "bhavatv evam. āgacchatu bhavān. ko doṣaḥ. paśyatu tāvad vāraṇêndram" iti.
children.translated_text: —with canopies spread all around, with their favored deities worshipped in front—he observed the stable adorned with horses dear to kings. With his heart seized by curiosity, having passed a little further, he saw from afar, indistinctly, the elephant stable—which seemed to leave no room in the sky due to its extreme height as if measured by a trunk, surrounded on all sides by a great plantain grove, filled from every direction by streams of rut-fluid flowing down like rivers made of bees, smearing the sense of smell from afar with a fragrance spreading in every direction as if from blooming <s>bakula</s> groves. And he asked: 'What does the lord do here?' The other replied: 'This indeed is the lord's mount—his external heart, his self born in another species, his life-breaths dwelling outside, his companion in the sport of valor—the lord of elephants named <s>Darpaśāta</s> (Destroyer of Pride), a name true to its meaning. This great pavilion that is seen is his resting-hall.' He said to him: 'Good sir! <s>Darpaśāta</s> is famous indeed. If so, let me first see the lord of elephants without fault. Therefore, please bring me there. I am exceedingly overcome by curiosity.' The other replied: 'So be it. Let the gentleman come. What harm is there? See the lord of elephants.'

children.translated_text: —making tawny a pond-like expanse netted with lotuses, discharging the deeply entered fourth state [of musth] like a deeply plunged lake; ceaselessly indicating as it were the auspicious commencement of entry into the fifth state with deep drum-sounds of ear-flap slapping that aroused the suspicion of ornamental garlands; as if lightening its weight from fear of splitting the earth, with the swaying of its long body-expanse through the rhythms of graceful dance in ceaseless, varied three-step movements; as if scratching its body against the cliff-walls of the directions; as if challenging the guardian elephants of the quarters with its trunk raised for battle; as if splitting the pillar of <s>Brahmā</s> with a thick, sharp tusk-blade held in its trunk; not fitting within the interior of the world, as if striving to emerge outside; scattered about as if with forests accumulated by long familiarity, with attendants gracefully adorned with fresh sprout-creepers on all sides; and delighted by the appropriate warm-season ministrations provided by attendant-elephants like lakes with waters dappled with moss, lotus-fiber, and tendrils; moreover, barring as it were the entire circle of the quarters including their mountain-ranges, oceans, islands, and forests, with an exceedingly thick trunk used as a bolt-bar, its belly rippled with fine wrinkle-ring-lines like tallies counting numerous battle-victories, far-flung by the wind of rival elephants' rut-fluid; with one tusk having its base sprinkled by spray contained within a plantain-stalk with a lotus-leaf placed in the hollow of its trunk; bearing the other tusk-shaft as if bristling with goosebumps of battle-excitement, appearing like a released sprout with a playfully dangling network of lotus-fibers; and with the spreading radiance of the pair of tusks, as if disgorging in many ways the groves of night-lilies savored during lake-sport,

children.translated_text: as if bestowing upon the directions heaps of its own fame; as if mocking lions who are clumsily skilled only at tearing apart wretched little insects; and as if fashioning for itself a face-veil of wish-fulfilling-tree silk; and raining down as if swallowed red lotus-groves, through the tender, delicate, red-cloth-soft palate visible during the playful raising of the trunk-shaft; as if disgorging heaps of fresh sprouts; as if vomiting with its naturally tawny eye the honey-nectar drunk from lotus-morsels; again and again releasing from both temples, on the pretext of thick rut-fluid fragrance, as if enjoyed <s>pārijātaka</s> groves mixed with <s>cūta</s> (mango), <s>campaka</s>, <s>lavalī</s>, <s>lavaṅga</s> (clove), <s>kakkola</s>, and <s>elā</s> (cardamom) creepers, combined with <s>sahakāra</s> (grafted mango) and filled with <s>karpūra</s> (camphor); day and night, as if earning the forests of all elephant-lords through rut-fluid charters inscribed by scratching with half-broken sugarcane stalks held in playful trunk-positions, made vocal by swarms of bees; being cooled by a shower-piece made of hail-stone fragments dripping with copious water-drops, like an ornamental garland-string of playful stars; bearing its head most high, as if resplendent with the coronation-turban of sovereignty over all elephant-lords; again and again fanning as it were, with devotion to its master, the royal <s>Lakṣmī</s> seated on the couch of its tusks, with ear-flap fans that alternately covered and revealed the faces of the directions;

children.text: gajâdhipatya-cihnena cāmareṇêva calatā vāladhinā virājamānam, sv-accha-śiśira-śīkara-cchalena dig-vijaya-pītāḥ sarita iva punaḥ-punar mukhena muñcantam, kṣaṇam avadhāna-dāna-niḥspandī-kṛta-sakalâvayavānām anya-dvirada-ḍiṇḍimâkarṇanâṅga-valanānām ante dīrgha-phūt-kāraiḥ paribhava-duḥkham ivâvedayantam, a-labdha-yuddham ivâtmānam anuśocantam, ārohâdhirūḍhi-paribhavena lajjamānam ivâṅgulī-likhita-mahī-talam, madaṃ muñcantam, avajñā-gṛhīta-mukta-kavala-kupitârohâraṭanânurodhena mada-tandrī-nimīlita-netra-tri-bhāgam, kathaṃ katham api manda-mandam an-ādarād ādadānaṃ kavalān, ardha-jagdha-tamāla-pallava-sruta-śyāmala-rasena prabhūtatayā mada-pravāham iva mukhenâpy utsṛjantam, calantam iva darpeṇa, śvasantam iva śauryeṇa, mūrcchantam iva madena, truṭyantam iva tāruṇyena, dravantam iva dānena, valgantam iva balena, mādyantam iva mānena, udyantam ivôtsāhena, tāmyantam iva tejasā, limpantam iva lāvaṇyena, siñcantam iva saubhāgyena, snigdhaṃ nakheṣu, paruṣaṃ roma-viṣaye, guruṃ mukhe, sac-chiṣyaṃ vinaye, mṛduṃ śirasi, dṛḍhaṃ paricayeṣu, hrasvaṃ skandha-bandhe, dīrgham āyuṣi, daridram udare, satata-pravṛttaṃ dāne, bala-bhadraṃ mada-līlāsu, kula-kalatram āyattatāsu, jinaṃ kṣamāsu, vahni-varṣaṃ krodha-mokṣeṣu, garuḍaṃ nāgôddhṛtiṣu, nāradaṃ
children.translated_text: resplendent with a swaying tail like a hereditary chowrie—the insignia of sovereignty over elephants—inherited through a long lineage; again and again releasing from its mouth, on the pretext of cool, clear spray, the rivers as if drunk during conquest-campaigns; for a moment having made all its limbs motionless through the gift of attention to the kettledrums of rival elephants, then turning its body, and at the end expressing as it were the grief of humiliation through long-drawn-out trumpeting blasts; as if lamenting itself for not having obtained battle; as if ashamed from the indignity of being mounted by a rider, scratching the ground-surface with its toe-nails; releasing rut-fluid; with one-third of its eyes closed in rut-drowsiness, in compliance with the clamoring of its angry rider whose food-morsel it had disdainfully seized and then released; somehow, very slowly, accepting morsels with indifference; discharging even from its mouth as it were a stream of rut-fluid in abundance, through the blackish-green juice flowing from half-eaten <s>tamāla</s> leaves; as if moving with pride, as if breathing with heroism, as if swooning with rut, as if bursting with youthfulness, as if flowing with rut-fluid, as if prancing with strength, as if intoxicated with honor, as if rising with zeal, as if burning with splendor, as if anointing with beauty, as if sprinkling with good fortune; smooth at the nails, rough in the area of body-hair, weighty in the face, well-disciplined in obedience, soft on the head, firm in familiarities, short in the shoulder-joint, long in lifespan, lean in the belly, ever-flowing in generosity, <s>Balabhadra</s>-like in rut-sport, of noble lineage in matters of dependence, a <s>Jina</s> in forbearance, a rain of fire in the release of anger, a <s>Garuḍa</s> in uprooting serpents, a <s>Nārada</s>

children.translated_text: in curiosity for quarrels, a dry thunderbolt in onslaughts, a <s>Makara</s> (sea-monster) in agitating armies, a venomous serpent in the work of biting, a <s>Varuṇa</s> in dragging with the noose of its trunk, a snare of <s>Yama</s> in entangling enemies in deadly embrace, <s>Kāla</s> (Time) in bringing things to maturity, <s>Rāhu</s> in seizing with its fierce grasp, <s>Lohitāṅga</s> (Mars) in crooked courses, a whirling firebrand in the knowledge of circular maneuvers; a wish-fulfilling gem-mountain for the fulfillment of valor's desires, a palace of tusk-pearl-mountain-pillar residences for its pride, a pleasure-vehicle of spontaneous movement adorned with bells, chowries, and ornaments—delighting the mind—for its spiritedness, a rain-house of rut-fluid streams creating the darkness of overcast days for its anger, a great temple with golden images for its ego, a pleasure-mountain with cascading streams from its temple-mounds for its arrogance, a diamond-palace with tusk-gateways for its haughtiness, a moving mountain-fortress formidable with high dome-turrets of its frontal boss for the kingdom, an iron rampart pierced by a thousand arrow-holes for the earth, a <s>pārijātaka</s> tree of the earth's paradise buzzing with the twang of hundreds of arrows for the realm, and also a concert-hall for the <s>tāṇḍava</s> dances of its ear-flaps, a drinking-pavilion for the circles of bees, an inner palace for the ornaments of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic sentiment), a festival of <s>Madana</s> (Love-god) for the graceful dances of its rut-play, an unbroken twilight for the garland-circles of stars, an untimely rainy season for the floods of the great rivers of rut-fluid, a false autumn season for the fragrances of <s>saptacchada</s>

And in his mind arose [the thought]: 'Surely mountains were ground to atoms in the making of this one. Whence else this weightiness? This is a marvel. These are the tusks of <s>Vindhya</s>, this the trunk of the primeval <s>Varāha</s> (Boar).' While he marveled thus, the door-keeper spoke:

body.translated_text: Having gone to that place, from afar itself [he saw the elephant]—making an untimely clamor with deep-throated roars, with flocks of <s>cātaka</s> birds in the sky and families of palace peacocks on the ground, their faces vocal with the cacophony of melodious <s>kekā</s> cries; the grounds filled with a fragrance of rut-liquor rivaling that of blooming <s>kadamba</s> blossoms; as if the dark season of untimely rain-clouds had taken bodily form; with abundant drops of honey—

children.text: -vṛtam, āsannôpaviṣṭa-viśiṣṭêṣṭa-lokam, hari-candana-rasa-prakṣālite tuṣāra-śīkara-śītala-tale danta-pāṇḍura-pāde śaśimaya iva muktā-śaila-śilā-paṭṭa-śayane samupaviṣṭam, śayanīya-paryanta-vinyaste samarpita-sakala-vigraha-bhāraṃ bhuje, diṅ-mukha-visarpiṇi deha-prabhā-vitāne vitata-maṇi-mayūkhe gharma-samaya-subhage sarasîva mṛdu-mṛṇāla-jāla-jaṭila-jale sa-rājakaṃ ramamāṇam, tejasaḥ paramâṇubhir iva kevalair nirmitam, an-icchantam api balād āropayitum iva siṃhâsanam, sarvâvayaveṣu sarva-lakṣaṇair gṛhītam, gṛhīta-brahma-caryam āliṅgitaṃ rāja-lakṣamyā, pratipannâsi-dhārā-dhāraṇa-vratam a-visaṃvādinaṃ rāja-rṣim, viṣama-rāja-mārga-vinihita-pada-skhalana-bhiyêva su-lagnaṃ dharme, sakala-bhū-pāla-parityaktena bhītenêva labdha-vācā sarvâtmanā satyena sevyamānam, āsanna-vāra-vilāsinī-pratiyātanābhiś caraṇa-nakha-pātinībhir digbhir iva daśabhir vigrahâvarjitābhiḥ praṇamyamānam, dīrghair dig-anta-pātibhir dṛṣṭi-pātair loka-pālānāṃ kṛtâkṛtam iva pratyavekṣamāṇam,
children.translated_text: surrounded [by attendants], with distinguished and beloved persons seated nearby, seated upon a couch of pearl-stone slabs — as if made of moonlight — on a floor washed with yellow sandalwood paste, cool with frost-like dew-drops, its base white as teeth; his entire body's weight surrendered upon one arm placed at the edge of the couch; delighting as a king in the canopy of his body's radiance spreading toward the mouths of the directions, studded with jewel-rays — as in a lake dense with soft lotus-fiber networks, beautiful in the hot season; as if fashioned solely from the atoms of splendor; as if the throne were forcibly mounting him even against his will; marked on every limb with every [auspicious] sign; one who had embraced <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibacy) [yet was] embraced by royal Fortune; a <s>rājarṣi</s> (royal sage) who had undertaken the vow of bearing the sword's edge and was true [to his word]; firmly attached to <s>dharma</s> — as if from fear of stumbling on the treacherous royal path; served wholly by Truth — which had found a voice [in him], as if frightened because abandoned by all [other] kings; being bowed to by the ten directions — like [ten] bodiless [entities] falling at his toenails, [mimicking] the return-salutations of the courtesans near at hand; inspecting, as it were, the deeds and misdeeds of the <s>Lokapālas</s> (World-Guardians) with long glances falling to the ends of the directions.

children.text: maṇi-pāda-pīṭha-pṛṣṭha-pratiṣṭhita-kareṇôparigamanâbhyanujñāṃ mṛgyamāṇam iva divasa-kareṇa, bhūṣaṇa-prabhā-samutsāraṇa-baddha-paryanta-maṇḍalena pradakṣiṇī-kriyamāṇam iva divasena, a-pramaṇadbhir giribhir api dūyamānaṃ, śauryôṣmaṇā phenāyamānam iva candana-dhavalaṃ lāvaṇya-jaladhim udvahantam eka-rājyôrjityena, nija-pratibimbāny api nṛpa-cakra-cūḍā-maṇi-dhṛtāny a-sahamānam iva darpa-duḥkhâsikayā cāmarânila-nibhena bahudhêva śvasantīṃ rāja-lakṣmīṃ dadhānam, sakalam iva catuḥ-samudra-lāvaṇyam ādāyôtthitayā śriyā samupaśliṣṭam, ābharaṇa-maṇi-kiraṇa-prabhā-jāla-jāyamānānîndra-dhanuḥ-sahasrāṇîndra-prābhṛta-prahitāni vilabhamānam iva rājñāṃ saṃbhāṣaṇeṣu parityaktam api madhu varṣantam, kāvya-kathāsv a-pītam apy amṛtam udvamantam, visrambha-bhāṣiteṣv an-ākṛṣṭam api hṛdayaṃ darśayantam, prasādeṣu niścalām api śriyaṃ sthāne sthāne sthāpayantam, vīra-goṣṭhīṣu pulakitena kapola-sthalenânurāga-saṃdeśam ivôpāṃśu raṇa-śriyaḥ śṛṇvantam, atikrānta-subhaṭa-kalahâlāpeṣu sneha-vṛṣṭim iva dṛṣṭim iṣṭe kṛpāṇe pātayantam, parihāsa-smiteṣu guru-pratāpa-bhītasya rājakasya sv-accham āśayam iva daśanâṃśubhiḥ kathayantam, sakala-loka-hṛdaya-sthitam api nyāye tiṣṭhantam, a-gocare guṇānām a-bhūmau saubhāgyānām a-viṣaye vara-pradānānām a-śakya āśiṣām a-mārge mano-rathānām ati-dūre daivasyâ-diśy upamānānām a-sādhye dharmasyâ-dṛṣṭa-pūrve lakṣmyā mahattve sthitam, aruṇa-pāda-pallavena su-gata-mantharôruṇā vajrâyudha-
children.translated_text: as if being sought by the sun for permission to ascend higher, [the sun] having set its trunk upon the surface of his jeweled footstool; as if being circumambulated by the day, which had formed a circular boundary through the dispersion of the radiance of his ornaments; causing distress even to unshakeable mountains; bearing an ocean of charm white as sandalwood, as if foaming from the heat of his valor through the pride of sole sovereignty; unable to endure even his own reflections borne in the crest-jewels of the circle of kings — as if by a sword of arrogant anguish; bearing the royal Fortune who seemed to be sighing in many ways, like the breeze of the <s>cāmara</s>; being embraced by <s>Śrī</s> (Fortune), as though she had arisen having absorbed all the charm of the four oceans; seeming to receive as gifts from <s>Indra</s> the thousands of rainbows born from the web of rays of his ornament-jewels; raining sweetness — though in conversations with kings he had renounced [flattery]; spewing nectar undrunk — in poetic tales; revealing the heart though undrawn forth — in confidential speech; establishing immovable Fortune at place after place — in his favors; in assemblies of heroes, hearing, as it were, the love-message of battle-glory whispered through the hair standing on end on his cheek; in talks recounting past warrior-combats, casting his glance like a shower of affection upon his beloved sword; in playful smiles, as if revealing through tooth-rays the pure disposition of the vassal-king frightened by the gravity of [his] majesty; established in the heart of all people, yet standing [firmly] in righteousness; stationed in a greatness that is beyond the reach of virtues, beyond the realm of good fortune, beyond the domain of boon-giving, beyond the capacity of blessings, beyond the path of wishes, exceedingly far from [the reach of] fate, in a direction [inaccessible to] comparison, unattainable by <s>dharma</s>, never before seen by <s>Lakṣmī</s>; with a body having reddish tender foot-soles, slow-moving and reddish thighs [like] those of <s>Vajrāyudha</s> (<s>Indra</s>),

children.text: -niṣṭhura-prakoṣṭha-pṛṣṭhena vṛṣa-skandhena bhāsvad-bimbâdhareṇa prasannâvalokitena candra-mukhena kṛṣṇa-keśena vapuṣā sarva-devatâvatāram ivâikatra darśayantam, api ca māṃsala-mayūkha-mālā-malinita-mahī-tale mahati mahârhe māṇikya-mālā-maṇḍita-mekhale mahā-nīlamaye pāda-pīṭhe kali-kāla-śirasîva salīlaṃ vinyasta-vāma-caraṇam, ākrānta-kāliya-phaṇā-cakravālaṃ bālam iva puṇḍarīkâkṣam, kṣauma-pāṇḍureṇa caraṇa-nakha-dīdhiti-pratānena prasaratā mahīṃ mahā-devī-paṭṭa-bandhenêva mahimānam āropayantam, a-praṇata-loka-pāla-kopenêvâti-lohitau sakala-nṛ-pati-mauli-mālāsv ati-pītaṃ padma-rāga-ratnâtapam iva vamantau sarva-tejasvi-maṇḍalâstam-aya-saṃdhyām iva dhārayantāv a-śeṣa-rājaka-kusuma-śekhara-madhura-sa-srotāṃsîva sravantau samasta-sāmanta-sīmantôttaṃsa-srak-saurabha-bhrāntair bhramara-maṇḍalair a-mitrôttamâṅgair iva muhūrtam apy a-virahitau saṃvāhana-tatparāyāḥ śriyo vikaca-rakta-paṅkaja-vana-vāsa-bhavanānîva kalpayantau jalaja-śaṅkha-mīna-makara-sa-nātha-talatayā kathita-catur-ambhodhi-bhoga-cihnāv iva caraṇau dadhānam, diṅ-nāga-danta-musalābhyām iva vikaṭa-makara-mukha-pratibandha-bandhurābhyām udvela-lāvaṇya-payodhi-pravāhābhyām iva phenâhita-śobhābyāṃ kalā-candana-drumābhyām iva bhogi-maṇḍala-śiro-ratna-raśmi-rajyamāna-mūlābhyāṃ hṛdayâropita-bhū-bhāra-dhāraṇa-māṇikya-stambhābyām ūru-daṇḍābhyāṃ virājamānam, a-mṛta-phena-piṇḍa-pāṇḍunā mekhalā-maṇi-mayūkha-khacitena nitamba-bimba-vyāsaṅginā vimala-payo-dhautena netra-sūtra-niveśa-śobhinâdhara-vāsasā Vāsuki-nirmokeṇêva
children.translated_text: a rough back of the forearm, a bull-like shoulder, a lower lip [bright] as the orb of the sun, a moon-face with a serene gaze, and dark hair — as if displaying the incarnation of all deities in a single [form]; and moreover, upon the great, magnificent footstool made of sapphire, adorned with strings of rubies at its girdle, its ground-level darkened by the thick garlands of fleshy rays — his left foot playfully placed as if upon the head of the <s>Kali</s>-age; like the young <s>Puṇḍarīkākṣa</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) standing upon the circle of <s>Kāliya</s>'s hoods; with the spreading whiteness of toenail-radiance, [white] as linen, as if elevating the earth to the dignity of a queen-consort's head-band; the two feet — exceedingly red as if from anger at the world-guardians who had not bowed, excessively yellow among the garlands of crowns of all kings, vomiting as it were the heat of ruby gems, maintaining as it were the twilight of the setting of all luminous hosts, flowing as if with sweet streams from the flower-garlands on the heads of all feudatories, never for a moment separated from the circles of bees confused by the garland-fragrance of the hair-ornaments of all vassals — as if from the [severed] heads of enemies; fashioning as it were the lotus-forest residences for Fortune who was eager for massage, [those feet] indicating by the conch, fish, and <s>makara</s> marks on their soles, together with the lord [mark], as if declaring the insignia of the enjoyment of the four oceans.

children.text: mandaraṃ dyotamānam, a-ghanena sa-tārā-gaṇenôpari-kṛtena dvitīyâmbareṇa bhuvanâbhogam iva bhāsamānam, ibha-pati-daśana-musala-sahasrôllekha-kaṭhina-masṛṇenâparyāptâmbara-prathimnā vividha-vāhinī-saṃkṣobha-kalakala-saṃmarda-sahiṣṇunā Kailāsam iva mahatā sphaṭika-taṭenôruṇôraḥ-kapāṭena virājamānam, Śrī-Sarasvatyor uro-vadanôpabhoga-vibhāga-sūtreṇêva pātitena śeṣeṇêva ca tad-bhuja-stambha-vinyasta-samasta-bhū-bhāra-labdha-viśrānti-sukha-prasuptena hāra-daṇḍena parivalita-kaṃdharam. jīvitâvadhi-gṛhīta-sarvasva-mahā-dāna-dīkṣā-cīreṇêva hāra-muktā-phalānāṃ kiraṇa-nikareṇa prāvṛta-vakṣaḥ-sthalam, aja-jigīṣayā bālair bhujair ivâparaiḥ prarohadbhir bāhûpadhāna-śāyinyāḥ śriyāḥ karṇôtpala-madhu-rasa-dhārā-saṃtānair iva galadbhir bhuja-janmanaḥ pratāpasya nirgamana-mārgair ivâvir-bhavadbhir aruṇaiḥ keyūra-ratna-kiraṇa-daṇḍair ubhayataḥ prasārita-maṇimaya-pakṣa-vitānam iva māṇikya-mahī-dharam, sakala-lokâloka-mārgârgalena catur-udadhi-parikṣepa-khāta-śāta-kumbha-śilā-prākāreṇa sarva-rāja-haṃsa-bandha-vajra-pañjareṇa bhuvana-lakṣmī-praveśa-maṅgala-mahā-maṇi-toraṇenâti-dīrgha-dor-daṇḍa-yugalena diśāṃ dik-pālānāṃ ca yugapad-āyatim apaharantam, sôdarya-lakṣmī-cumbana-lobhena kaustubha-maṇer iva mukhâvayavatāṃ gatasyâdharasya galatā rāgeṇa pārijāta-pallava-rasenêva siñcantaṃ diṅ-mukhāni, antarântarā suhṛt-parihāsa-smitaiḥ prakīryamāṇa-vimala-daśana-śikhā-pratānaiḥ prakṛti-mūḍhāyā rāja-śriyāḥ prajñâlokam iva darśayantam, mukha-janitêndu-saṃdehâgatāni kumudinī-vanānîva preṣayantam, sphuṭa-sphaṭika-dhavala-daśana-paṅkti-kṛta-kumuda-vana-śaṅkā-praviṣṭāṃ śaraj-jyotsnām iva visarjayantam, madirâmṛta-pārijāta-gandha-garbheṇa bharita-sakala-kakubhā mukhâmodenâmṛta-mathana-divasam iva sṛjantam, vikaca-mukha-kamala-ka-
children.translated_text: shining like <s>Mandara</s> [mountain] with its lower garment — white as undried nectar-foam, studded with girdle-gem rays, clinging to the hip-globe, washed clean by pure water, beautified by the placement of the drawstring — [resembling] the sloughed skin of <s>Vāsuki</s>; appearing with a second sky — cloudless, with a host of stars, placed above — as if [displaying] the expanse of the universe; shining with a broad, radiant chest-door like <s>Kailāsa</s>, with a great crystal surface — smooth yet hard as if scratched by thousands of elephant-lord tusk-pestles, of immeasurable sky-like breadth, enduring the tumultuous crushing clamor of diverse armies; his neck encircled by a string of pearls — like the remainder of <s>Śeṣa</s> (the serpent) [coiled around him], laid down as if the dividing thread between <s>Śrī</s> (Fortune) and <s>Sarasvatī</s> for the enjoyment of chest and face, [or] as if having fallen asleep in the bliss of rest having deposited the entire burden of the earth upon his arm-pillars; his chest-surface covered by a mass of pearl-necklace rays — as if by a bark-garment of the great initiation of life-long all-surrendering generosity; seeming like a ruby-mountain with jewel-wing-canopies extended on both sides, through the red armlet-gem ray-staffs appearing — like pathways for the emergence of valor born from his arms, like streams of ear-lotus honey dripping from Fortune who sleeps on the pillow of his arms, like other young arms sprouting as if from desire to conquer [the world].

children.text: -rṇikā-kośenân-avaratam āpīyamāna-śvāsa-saurabham ivâdho-mukhena nāsā-vaṃśena, cakṣuṣaḥ kṣīra-snigdhasya dhavalimnā diṅ-mukhāny a-pūrva-vadana-candrôdayôdvela-kṣīrôdôtplāvitānîva kurvāṇam, vimala-kapola-phalaka-pratibimbitāṃ cāmara-grāhiṇīṃ vigrahiṇīm iva mukha-nivāsinīṃ Sarasvatīṃ dadhānam, aruṇena cūḍā-maṇi-śociṣā Sarasvatîrṣyā-kupita-Lakṣmī-prasādana-lagnena caraṇâlaktakenêva lohitâyata-lalāṭa-taṭam, āpāṭalâṃśu-tantrī-saṃtāna-valayinīṃ kuṇḍala-maṇi-kuṭila-koṭi-bāla-vīṇām an-avarata-calita-caraṇānāṃ vādayatām upavīṇayatām iva svara-vyākaraṇa-viveka-viśāradam, śravaṇâvataṃsa-madhu-kara-kulānāṃ kala-kvaṇitam ākarṇayantam, utphulla-mālatīmayena rāja-lakṣmyāḥ kaca-graha-līlâlagnena nakha-jyotsnā-valayenêva mukha-śaśi-pariveṣa-maṇḍalena muṇḍa-mālā-guṇena parikalita-keśântam, śikhaṇḍâbharaṇa-bhuvā muktā-phalâlokena marakata-maṇi-kiraṇa-kalāpena cânyonya-saṃvalana-vṛjinena prayāga-pravāha-veṇikā-vāriṇêvâgatya svayam abhiṣicyamānam, śrama-jala-vilīna-bahala-kṛṣṇāguru-paṅka-tilaka-kalaṅka-kalpitena kālimnā prārthanā-cāṭu-catura-caraṇa-patana-śata-śyāmikā-kiṇenêva nīlāyamāna-lalāṭêndu-lekhābhiḥ kṣubhita-mānasôdgatair utkalikā-kalāpair iva hārair ullasadbhir avaṣṭabhyamānābhir vilāsa-valgana-caṭulair bhrū-latā-kalpair īrṣyayā śriyam iva tarjayantībhir āyāmibhiḥ svasitair a-virala-parimalair Malaya-mārutamayaiḥ pāśair ivâkarṣantībhir vikaṭa-bakulâvalī-varāṭaka-veṣṭita-mukhai-
children.translated_text: with the nose-bridge — down-turned, as if incessantly drinking in the fragrance of breath from the seed-cup of the blossoming lotus of his face; making the mouths of the directions appear as if flooded by the overflowing milk-ocean agitated by the unprecedented rising of his face-moon, through the whiteness of his milky-smooth gaze; bearing <s>Sarasvatī</s> — dwelling in his face, reflected in his spotless cheek-panels — as if embodied [and serving as] a <s>cāmara</s>-bearer; his forehead-surface reddened by the glow of the crest-jewel — as if by the lac-dye on the foot of <s>Lakṣmī</s> angered by jealousy of <s>Sarasvatī</s>; as if hearing the melodious humming of the bee-swarms on his ear-ornaments — which seemed to be accompanying like secondary <s>vīṇās</s>, [being] young <s>vīṇās</s> with curved crests of earring-gems, with circling strings of pale-pink rays — [he], skilled in discriminating the grammar of musical notes among those who constantly play with moving feet; his hair-ends encircled by a garland of skulls — [which is really] the halo of moon-face, the circle of nail-lustre, attached in the playful tussle of hair-grasping by royal Fortune, made of full-blown <s>mālatī</s> (jasmine); being self-anointed, as it were, by waters resembling the <s>Prayāga</s> (confluence) stream-braid, created by the mutual intertwining fault of the emerald-gem-ray clusters and the pearl-lustre from the peacock-feather ornament;

children.text: -r bṛhadbhiḥ stana-kalaśaiḥ sva-dāra-saṃtoṣa-rasam ivâ-śeṣam uddharantībhiḥ kucôtkampikā-vikāra-preṅkhitānāṃ hāra-tarala-maṇīnāṃ raśmibhir ākṛṣya hṛdayam iva haṭhāt praveśayantībhiḥ prabhā-mucām ābharaṇa-maṇīnāṃ mayūkhaiḥ prasāritair bahubhir iva bāhubhir āliṅgantībhir jṛmbhânubandha-bandhura-vadanâravindâvaraṇī-kṛtair uttānaiḥ kara-kisalayaiḥ sa-rabhasa-pradhāvitāni mānasānîva nirundhatībhir madanândha-madhu-kara-kula-kīryamāṇa-karṇa-kusuma-rajaḥ-kaṇa-kūṇita-koṇāni kusuma-śara-śara-nikara-prahāra-mūrcchâmukulitānîva locanāni caturaṃ saṃcārayantībhir anyonya-matsarād āvir-bhavad-bhaṅghura-bhrukuṭi-vibhrama-kṣiptaiḥ kaṭâkṣaiḥ karṇêndīvarāṇîva tāḍayantībhir a-nimeṣa-darśana-sukha-rasa-rāśiṃ mantharita-pakṣmaṇā cakṣuṣā pītam iva komala-kapola-pālī-pratibimbitaṃ vahantībhir abhilāṣa-līlā-nir-nimitta-smitaiś candrôdayān iva madana-sahāyakāya saṃpādayantībhir aṅga-bhaṅga-valanânyonya-ghaṭitôttānakara-veṇikābhiḥ sphuṭana-mukharâṅgulī-kāṇḍa-kuṇḍalī-kriyamāṇa-nakha-dīdhiti-nivaha-nibhenâ-kiñ-cit-kara-Kāma-kārmukāṇîva ruṣā bhañjantībhir vāra-vilāsinībhir vilupyamāna-saubhāgyam iva sarvataḥ, sparśa-svinna-vepamāna-kara-kisalaya-galita-caraṇâravindāṃ caraṇa-grāhiṇīṃ vihasya koṇena līlā-lasaṃ śirasi tāḍayantam, an-avarata-kara-kalita-koṇatayā câtmanaḥ priyāṃ vīṇām iva Śriyam api śikṣayantam, niḥ-sneha iti dhanaiḥ, an-āśrayaṇīya iti doṣaiḥ, nigraha-rucir itîndriyaiḥ, dur-upasarpa iti kalinā, nīrasa iti vyasanaiḥ, bhīrur ity a-yaśasā, dur-graha-citta-vṛttir iti citta-bhuvā, strī-para iti Sarasvatyā, ṣaṇḍha iti para-kalatraiḥ, kāṣṭhā-munir iti yatibhiḥ, dhūrta iti veśyābhiḥ, neya iti suhṛdbhiḥ, karma-kara iti
children.translated_text: by the court ladies — who with their large pitcher-like breasts seemed to be drawing out completely the essence of contentment with one's own wife; who with the rays of the trembling gems of necklaces swinging from the agitation of their breast-ornaments seemed to forcibly pull out and enter his heart; who with the many extended beams of their radiance-emitting ornament-jewels seemed to embrace [him] with many arms; who with their upturned lotus-bud-like hands — made into screens for their lotus-faces made lovely by the contortion of yawning — seemed to be blocking the minds that had rushed forth impetuously; who skillfully moved their eyes — their corners narrowed by pollen-particles from ear-flowers scattered by swarms of bees blind with passion — [eyes] as if closed in a swoon from the rain of the Flower-armed One's (<s>Kāma</s>'s) arrows; who with sidelong glances cast through the play of arching furrowed eyebrows appearing from mutual jealousy seemed to strike [him] like ear-lotuses; who bore his [reflection] drunk as it were — through unblinking eyes churning with the relish of bliss of gazing — reflected on their soft cheek-surfaces; who with purposeless smiles of playful longing seemed to produce moonrises as allies of <s>Madana</s> (Love); who with intertwined upturned-palm braids formed by the bending and turning of their limbs, with nail-radiance-clusters [shining] from cracking-resounding finger-joints coiled [like earrings] — seemed to be angrily breaking miniature bows of <s>Kāma</s> made of [mere] fingertips — by such court ladies his beauty was being plundered from all sides; laughing and playfully striking on the head with a corner-glance the one who had grasped his foot — her lotus-hand trembling, sweating from the touch; and through the constant [playing of] the <s>koṇa</s> (plectrum) held in his hand, instructing his beloved <s>Vīṇā</s> — and Fortune as well; children.translated_text: Moreover, for his generosity, supplicants [are the limit]; for his wisdom, the scriptures; for his poetic power, words; for his courage, the domains of daring; for his enthusiasm, undertakings; for his fame, the mouths of the directions; for his love, the hearts of the people; for the multitude of his virtues, counting; for his skill, the arts—none of these are adequate domains. And in this king, the <s>yoga-paṭṭakas</s> (yoga-seats) of ascetics [find new meaning], the earthen figures of painters [gain royal forms], the quarrels of bees over giving and receiving [are mirrored], the foot-divisions of poetic meters [are manifest], the four-division arrangements of the chessboard [find parallel], the enmity of serpents toward the twice-born elder [<s>Garuḍa</s>, is reflected], the investigations of topics by logicians [find their subject]"—thus reflecting, he approached, and wearing his sacred thread across his chest, made the auspicious greeting of <s>svasti</s>.

body.translated_text: And having seen him—as if blessed, as if restrained, as if filled with longing, as if satiated—with a face releasing goosebumps, shedding drops of joyful tears, smiling with wonder from afar itself, he reflected: "This is he—of noble birth, of well-assumed name, a mass of splendors, lord of the household of the field bounded by four oceans, enjoyer of the fruit of the pillar of <s>Brahmā</s>, chief wrestler of victory surpassing the deeds of all primordial kings—the divine Supreme Lord <s>Harṣa</s>. By him indeed does the earth possess a king. His childhood deeds are not hostile to the Bull [of <s>Dharma</s>] as are those of <s>Hari</s>; his displays of lordship do not cause distress to <s>Dakṣa</s>'s people as do those of <s>Paśupati</s> (<s>Śiva</s>); there are no rumors betraying the destruction of clans as with <s>Śatakratu</s> (<s>Indra</s>); his seizings of the rod of punishment are not excessively zealous as with <s>Yama</s>; his treasure-houses are not guarded by thousands of sword-wielding crocodiles as with <s>Varuṇa</s>; his acquisitions of treasure are not barren as with <s>Dhanada</s> (<s>Kubera</s>); his philosophical views are not devoid of purposeful discourse as with <s>Jina</s>; his splendors are not marred by manifold defects as with the moon. Wondrous is this kingship that surpasses even the immortals'—

But when that one, by his silence, did not respond to the king's words, and the entire court was mute, <s>Bāṇa</s>, standing silent as if for a moment, addressed the king: "My lord! As if ignorant of the truth, as if incredulous, as if easily led, as if unaware of the ways of the world—why does Your Majesty command thus? The natural dispositions and rumors of the world are wayward and varied. But the great must see things as they truly are. You should not regard me otherwise, as if I were undistinguished. I am a Brahmin, born in the <s>soma</s>-drinking lineage of the <s>Vātsyāyanas</s>. The <s>saṃskāras</s> (sacraments) beginning with <s>upanayana</s> (sacred thread investiture) were performed at the proper times. The <s>Veda</s> with its limbs was properly studied. And scriptures were heard to the extent of my ability. Through marriage I am a householder. In love there was serpent-like fickleness. But my childhood was indeed not free from follies that violate the interests of both worlds. In this I make no denial. And indeed my heart feels as if seized with remorse on account of this very thing. But now, when one whose mind is at peace like a <s>Sugata</s> (<s>Buddha</s>), who is like <s>Manu</s> the creator of the rules of the <s>varṇāśrama</s> (caste and life-stage) system, and who is like the visible rod-bearer (<s>Yama</s>) himself, rules this earth girdled by seven oceans with all its island-garlands—who would, even in thought, dare to enact the pantomime of unruliness, the friend of all vices? And he reflected in his mind: "Exceedingly gracious indeed is Lord <s>Harṣa</s>, that even though angered by the reputation of my many youthful indiscretions, he still feels affection for me in his heart. If I were in his sight constantly, he would not show favor at my mere appearance. But he wishes me to be virtuous. For masters instruct their dependents in discipline through the manner of their treatment, even without words. Moreover, shame on me—blinded by my own faults, distressed by disregard—thinking this way and that about

And within just a few days, by the king with supreme affection, he was brought to the highest pinnacle of favor-born honor, esteem, love, trust, wealth, humor, and influence.

body.translated_text: His kinsmen, exceedingly delighted at the extraordinary honor received from the king, departed praising him. And gradually—saluting some, being saluted by others, being kissed on the head by some, smelling some on the crown, being embraced by some, embracing others, being blessed by some, bestowing blessings on others—standing amidst his many kinsmen, he rejoiced greatly. He took a seat brought by the bustling servants while the elders were seated. And receiving worship with offerings and other honors, he was exceedingly delighted. With a pleased mind he asked them all: "Have you all been well during these many days? Are the sacrificial rites performed without obstruction, with the circle of <s>dvijas</s> (twice-born) satisfied by proper fees? Do the sacred fires consume the oblations with unimpaired <s>mantras</s> as prescribed? Do the young students study at the proper times? Is the daily study of the <s>Vedas</s> uninterrupted? Is the same ancient devotion to sacrificial lore maintained? Are there still those same lecture circles in <s>vyākaraṇa</s> (grammar) where mutual rivalry made every day fruitful? Is there still the same ancient assembly for the discussion of authoritative texts, having set aside all other business? Is there still the same excess of relish for <s>Mīmāṃsā</s> that made the flavor of other <s>śāstras</s> fade? Are there still those same poetic discourses raining the nectar of fresh well-composed verses?"

Thus there is no kingship without blemish except that of the god of gods, lord of all the continents, <s>Harṣa</s>. For many wonders are heard of him. Namely: here, mountains with wings were conquered by might and rendered immovable. Here, by the lord of creatures, the earth was placed upon the coils of <s>Śeṣa</s>. Here, by the supreme being,

children.text: sindhu-rājaṃ pramathya lakṣmīr ātmī-kṛtā. atra balinā mocita-bhūbhṛd-veṣṭano mukto mahā-nāgaḥ. atra devenâbhiṣiktaḥ kumāraḥ. atra svāminâika-prahāra-prapatitârātinā prakhyāpitā śaktiḥ. atra nara-siṃhena sva-hasta-viśasitârātinā prakaṭī-kṛto vikramaḥ. atra paramêśvareṇa tuṣāra-śaila-bhuvo durgāyā gṛhītaḥ karaḥ. atra loka-nāthena diśāṃ mukheṣu parikalpitā loka-pālāḥ, sakala-bhuvana-kośaś câgra-janmanāṃ vibhaktaḥ, ity evam-ādayaḥ prathama-kṛta-yugasyêva dṛśyante mahā-samārambhāḥ. ato 'sya su-gṛhīta-nāmnaḥ puṇya-rāśeḥ pūrva-puruṣa-vaṃśânukrameṇâditaḥ prabhṛti caritam icchāmaḥ śrotum. su-mahān kālo naḥ śuśrūṣamāṇānām. ayaskānta-maṇaya iva lohāni nīrasa-niṣṭhurāṇi kṣullakānām apy ākarṣanti manāṃsi mahatāṃ guṇāḥ, kim uta sva-bhāva-sarasa-mṛdūnîtareṣām. kasya na dvitīya-mahā-bhārate bhaved asya carite kutūhalam? ācaṣṭāṃ bhavān. bhavatu Bhārgavo 'yaṃ vaṃśaḥ
children.translated_text: having churned the lord of the ocean, <s>Lakṣmī</s> was made his own. Here, by the powerful one, the great serpent was freed from the encirclement of mountains. Here, by the god, the prince was consecrated. Here, by the lord who felled enemies with a single blow, his <s>śakti</s> (power) was made manifest. Here, by the man-lion, who slew enemies with his own hands, his valor was displayed. Here, by the supreme lord, the hand of <s>Durgā</s>, daughter of the snowy mountain, was taken. Here, by the lord of the world, guardians of the quarters were appointed at the faces of the directions, and the treasury of the entire world was distributed among the first-born—such and similar great undertakings are seen as if belonging to the first <s>Kṛtayuga</s>. Therefore we wish to hear the story of this one of auspicious name, this mass of merit, from the very beginning in the order of his ancestral lineage. Long indeed have we been waiting eagerly. Like lodestones attracting iron—the tasteless, hard things—the virtues of great men attract even the minds of the small, how much more the naturally tender hearts of others? Who would not be curious about his story, which is like a second <s>Mahābhārata</s>? Let the lord narrate it. May this lineage of <s>Bhārgava</s>

children.text: śucinânena puṇya-rāja-rṣi-carita-śravaṇena sutarāṃ śucitaraḥ," ity evam abhidhāya tūṣṇīm abhūt.
children.translated_text: become even more pure through the hearing of this holy story of the royal sages," and having spoken thus, he fell silent.

body.translated_text: Then the youngest among them, <s>Śyāmala</s> by name, with eyes long as lotus petals, dearer to <s>Bāṇa</s> than his very life-breath and its master, having received the signal from the others, spoke affectionately, his face like a moon bathing the quarters in the moonlight of his teeth: "Father <s>Bāṇa</s>! The king among <s>dvijas</s> (twice-born) took the hand of his guru's wife. <s>Purūravas</s> was separated from his beloved <s>Āyus</s> through greed for Brahmin wealth. <s>Nahuṣa</s>, through desire for another's wife, became a great serpent.

body.text: Bāṇas tu vihasyâbravīt: "ārya! na yukty-anurūpam abhihitam. a-ghaṭamāna-mano-ratham iva bhavatāṃ kutūhalam avakalpayāmi. śakyâśakya-parisaṃkhyāna-śūnyāḥ prāyeṇa svârtha-tṛṣaḥ. para-guṇânurāgiṇī priya-jana-kathā-śravaṇa-rasa-rabhasa-mohitā ca manye mahatām api matir apaharati pravivekam. paśyatv āryaḥ kva paramâṇu-parimāṇaṃ baṭu-hṛdayam, kva samasta-brahma-stambha-vyāpi devasya caritam? kva parimita-varṇa-vṛttayaḥ katipaye śabdāḥ, kva saṃkhyâtigās tad-guṇāḥ? sarva-jñasyâpy ayam a-viṣayaḥ, Vācaspater apy a-gocaraḥ, Sarasvatyā apy ati-bhāraḥ, kim utâsmad-vidhasya? kaḥ khalu puruṣâyuṣa-śatenâpi śaknuyād a-vikalam asya caritaṃ varṇayitum? Eka-deśe tu yadi kutūhalaṃ vaḥ, sajjā vayam. Iyam adhigata katipayâkṣara-lava-laghīyasī jihvā kvôpayogaṃ gamiṣyati? bhavantaḥ śrotāraḥ. vaṇyate Harṣa-caritam. kim anyat. adya tu pariṇata-prāyo divasaḥ. paścāl lambamāna-kapila-kiraṇa-jaṭâbhāra-bhāsvaro bhagavān bhārgavo Rāma iva samanta-pañcaka-rudhira-mahā-hrade nimajjati saṃdhyā-rāga-paṭale Pūṣā. śvo nivedayitâsmi" iti. sarve ca te "tathā" iti pratyapadyanta. nâti-cirād utthāya saṃdhyām upāsituṃ Śoṇam ayāsīt.
body.translated_text: But <s>Bāṇa</s> laughed and said: "Noble sir! What you have said does not accord with reason. I consider your curiosity to be like an unfulfillable desire. Those thirsting for their own purposes are generally devoid of any reckoning of what is possible and what is impossible. And I think that the minds of even great men, enamored of others' virtues, intoxicated by the passionate eagerness to hear the tales of loved ones, lose their discrimination. Let the noble one consider: where is the minute heart of a young student, and where the story of the lord that pervades the entire pillar of <s>Brahman</s>? Where are a few words with limited letters and meters, and where his innumerable virtues? This is beyond the scope of even the omniscient, beyond the reach of even <s>Vācaspati</s>, too great a burden even for <s>Sarasvatī</s>—how much more so for one such as me? Who indeed, even in a hundred human lifetimes, could describe his story completely? But if you are curious about some portion, we are ready. Where else will this tongue, which has acquired but a small fragment of a few syllables, find its purpose? You are the listeners. The <s>Harṣacarita</s> shall be narrated. What more need be said? But today the day is mostly spent. In the west, the glorious <s>Bhārgava Rāma</s>, as it were, sinks into the great lake of blood at <s>Samantapañcaka</s>, resplendent with the mass of matted locks formed by his trailing tawny rays—<s>Pūṣan</s> sinks in the crimson veil of twilight. Tomorrow I shall narrate." And they all assented, saying "So be it." Before long, he arose and went to the <s>Śoṇa</s> river to perform the evening worship.

body.text: atha madhu-mada-pallavita-mālavī-kapola-komalâtape mukulite 'hni, kamalinī-mīlanād iva lohitatame tamo-lihi ravau lambamāne, ravi-ratha-

children.text: -turaga-mārgânusāreṇa Yama-mahiṣa iva dhāvati nabhasi tamasi, krameṇa ca gṛha-tāpasa-kuṭīraka-paṭalâvalambiṣu raktâtapa-cchedaiḥ saha saṃhṛteṣu valkaleṣu, kali-kalmaṣa-muṣi muṣṇati gaganam agni-hotra-dhāma-dhūme, sa-niyame yajamāna-jane mauna-vratini, vihāra-velā-vilole paryaṭati patnī-jane, vikīryamāṇa-harita-śyāmāka-śāli-pūlikāsu dugdhāsu homa-kapilāsu, hūyamāne vaitāna-tanūnapāti, pūta-viṣṭarôpaviṣṭe kṛṣṇâjina-jaṭile jaṭini japati baṭu-jane, brahmâsanâdhyāsini dhyāyati yogi-gaṇe, tāladhvani-dhāvamānân-antânte-vāsini alasa-vṛddha-śrotriyânumatena galad-grantha-daṇḍakôdgāriṇi sadyāṃ samavadhārayati vaṭhara-viṭa-baṭu-samāje, samunmajjati ca jyotiṣi tārakâkhye khe, prāpte pradoṣârambhe bhavanam āgatyôpaviṣṭaḥ snigdhair bandhubhiś ca sārdha tayâiva goṣṭhyā tasthau. nīta-prathama-yāmaś ca Gaṇapater bhavane parikalpitaṃ śayanīyam asevata. itareṣāṃ tu sarveṣāṃ nimīlita-dṛśām apy an-upajāta-nidrāṇāṃ kamala-vanānām iva sūryôdayaṃ pratipālayatāṃ kutūhalena katham api sā kṣapā kṣayam agacchat.
children.translated_text: when darkness raced across the sky like <s>Yama</s>'s buffalo following the path of the sun's chariot-horses, and gradually the bark garments were gathered along with the red patches of sunlight clinging to the rows of ascetics' huts, when the smoke of the <s>agnihotra</s> fire's flames was stealing across the sky washing away the stains of the <s>Kali</s> age, when the sacrificing folk had observed their vows and fallen silent, when the wives strolled about in the pleasant evening hour, when the milch cows had been milked while scattering offerings of green <s>śyāmāka</s> and rice, when the sacrificial fire of <s>Tanūnapāt</s> was being offered, when the young students seated on sacred <s>kuśa</s> grass, clad in black deerskins with matted hair, were reciting their prayers, when the assembly of <s>yogis</s> was meditating seated in <s>brahmāsana</s>, when the crowd of rogues, rascals, and simpleton students at the far end of the settlement, with the approval of the lazy old scholars, was listening to the text-holder droning out sections at the sound of a cymbal—and when the luminous stars had risen in the sky and the time of early evening had arrived—he came home, sat down, and remained in that same company of affectionate kinsmen. When the first watch of the night had passed, he retired to the bed prepared at <s>Gaṇapati</s>'s house. But for all the others, though their eyes were closed, sleep would not come, and like lotus ponds waiting for sunrise, through their curiosity that night somehow came to an end.

body.translated_text: Then, when the day had closed its eyes in the heat soft as the cheek of a <s>Mālavī</s> creeper blossoming with spring's intoxication, when the sun, most ruddy, hung low as if from the closing of the lotus ponds, licking the darkness,

body.text: atha yāminyās turye yāme pratibuddhaḥ sa eva bandī śloka-dvayam agāyat:
body.translated_text: Then, in the fourth watch of the night, that same bard, having awakened, sang two verses:

children.text: "paścād aṅghriṃ prasārya trika-nati-vitataṃ drāghayitvâṅgam uccair
children.translated_text: "Stretching his hind leg back, extending his body high with the triple bending of his trunk,

body.text: Bāṇas tu tac chrutvā samutsṛjya nidrām utthāya prakṣālya vadanam upāsya ca bhagavatīṃ saṃdhyā-mudite ca bhagavati Savitari gṛhīta-tāmbūlas tatrâivâtiṣṭhat. atrântare sarve 'sya jñātayaḥ samājagmuḥ, parivārya câsāṃ-cakrire. asāv api pūrvôddhātena viditâbhiprāyas teṣāṃ puro Harṣa-caritaṃ kathayitum ārebhe:
body.translated_text: <s>Bāṇa</s>, hearing that, casting off sleep, rising, washing his face, worshipping the blessed <s>Sandhyā</s> (twilight), and when the blessed <s>Savitṛ</s> (Sun) was gladdened by the <s>Sandhyā</s>, having taken his betel, stood right there. Meanwhile, all his kinsmen assembled and, surrounding him, sat down. And he, whose intention was already known from the previous portent, began to narrate the <s>Harṣacarita</s> before them:

body.text: śrūyatām: asti puṇya-kṛtām adhivāso vāsavâvāsa iva vasudhām avatīrṇaḥ satatam-a-saṃkīrṇa-varṇa-vyavahāra-sthitiḥ kṛta-yuga-vyavasthaḥ, sthala-kamala-bahalatayā potrônmūlyamāna-mṛṇālair udgīta-medinī-sāra-guṇair iva kṛta-madhu-kara-kolāhalair halair ullikhyamāna-kṣetraḥ, kṣīrôda-payaḥpāyi-payoda-siktābhir iva puṇḍrêkṣuvāṭa-saṃtatibhir nir-antaraḥ, prati-diśam a-pūrva-parvatakair iva khala-dhāna-dhāmabhir vibhajyamānaiḥ sasya-kūṭaiḥ saṃkaṭa-sakala-sīmântaḥ, samantād uddhāta-ghaṭī-sicyamānair jīraka-jūṭair jaṭilita-bhūmiḥ, urvarā-varīyobhiḥ śāleyair alaṃ-kṛtaḥ, pāka-viśarāru-rājamāṣa-nikara-kirmīritaiś ca sphuṭita-mudga-phala-kośī-kapiśitair go-dhūma-dhāmabhiḥ sthalī-pṛṣṭhair adhiṣṭhitaḥ, mahiṣa-pṛṣṭha-pratiṣṭhita-gāyad-gopāla-pālitaiś ca kīṭa-paṭala-lampaṭa-caṭakânusṛtair avaṭu-ghaṭita-ghaṇṭā-ghaṭī-raṭita-ramaṇīyair aṭadbhir aṭavīṃ Hara-vṛṣabha-pītam āmayâśaṅkayā bahudhā-vibhaktaṃ kṣīrôdam iva kṣīraṃ kṣaradbhir bāṣpa-

children.text: -cchedya-tṛṇa-tṛptair go-dhanair dhavalita-vipinaḥ, vividha-makha-homa-dhūmândha-śata-manyu-muktair locanair iva sahasra-saṃkhyaiḥ kṛṣṇa-śāraiḥ śārī-kṛtôddeśaḥ, dhavala-dhūli-mucā ketakī-vanānāṃ rajobhiḥ pāṇḍurī-kṛtaiḥ prathamôddhūlana-bhasma-dhūsaraiḥ śiva-purasyêva praveśaiḥ pradeśair upaśobhitaḥ, śāka-kandala-śyāmalita-grāmôpakaṇṭha-kāśyapī-pṛṣṭhaḥ, pade pade karabha-pālībhiḥ pīlu-pallava-prasphoṭitaiḥ kara-puṭa-pīḍita-komala-mātuluṅgī-dala-rasôpaliptaiḥ svêcchā-vicita-kuṅkuma-kesara-kṛta-puṣpa-prakaraiḥ pratyagra-phala-rasa-pāna-sukha-supta-pathikair vana-devatā-dīyamānâmṛta-rasa-prapā-gṛhair iva drākṣā-latā-maṇḍapaiḥ sphurat-phalānāṃ ca bīja-lagna-śuka-cañcu-rāgāṇām iva samārūḍha-kapi-kula-kapola-saṃdihyamāna-kusumānāṃ dāḍimīnāṃ vanair vilobhanīyôpanirgamaḥ, vana-pāla-pīyamāna-nārikela-rasâsavaiś ca pathika-loka-lupyamāna-piṇḍa-kharjūrair golâṅgūla-lihyamāna-madhurâmoda-piṇḍī-rasaiś cakora-cañcu-jarjaritârukair upavanair abhirāmaḥ, tuṅgârjuna-pālī-parivṛtaiś ca go-kulâvatāra-kaluṣita-kūla-kīlālair adhvaga-śata-śaraṇyair araṇya-varuṇa-dharā-bandhair a-vandhya-vana-randhraḥ, karabhīya-kumāraka-pālyamānair auṣṭrakair aurabhrakaiś ca kṛta-saṃbādhaḥ, diśi diśi ravi-ratha-turaga-vilobhanāyâiva viloṭhana-mṛdita-kuṅkuma-sthalī-rasa-samālabdhānām ut-protha-puṭair unmukhair udara-śāyi-kiśoraka-java-jananāya prabhañjanam iva câpibantīnāṃ vāta-hariṇīnām iva sva-cchanda-cāriṇīnāṃ vaḍavānāṃ vṛndair vicaradbhir ācitaḥ, an-avarata-kratu-dhūmândhakāra-pravṛttair haṃsa-yūthair iva guṇair dhavalita-bhuvanaḥ, saṃgīta-gata-muraja-rava-mattair mayūrair iva vibhavair mukharita-jīva-lokaḥ, śaśi-karâvadāta-vṛttair muktā-phalair iva guṇibhiḥ prasādhitaḥ, pathika-śata-vilupyamāna-sphīta-phalair mahā-tarubhir iva sarvâtithibhir abhi-
children.translated_text: —[milk]; whose forests are whitened by cattle; whose regions are made into a chessboard by thousands of black antelopes, like eyes released by the hundred-powered one (<s>Indra</s>) blinded by the smoke of various sacrificial offerings; beautified by localities that are, like entrances to <s>Śiva's</s> city, white with dust shed from <s>ketakī</s> groves, grey with preliminary ash-smearing — made pale by the pollen; whose nearby slopes of the <s>Kāśyapī</s> [river] are darkened by vegetable and tuber [gardens] near the village borders; charming in its outskirts at every step with grape-vine arbors — like ambrosia-distributing rest-houses offered by forest deities — where travelers sleep happily after drinking fresh fruit-juice, [decorated] with crushed <s>kuṅkuma</s>-stamen flower-offerings freely gathered, hands anointed with the juice of soft citron-leaves pressed in the hollow of the palm, with <s>pīlu</s>-shoot fragments [scattered about] by lines of young camels; delightful with orchards of pomegranate trees whose fruits have seeds marked with parrot-beak redness, whose flowers are doubtfully identified [as flowers or] with cheeks of monkey-troops that have climbed them; full of fruit; pleasant with gardens where forest-guards drink coconut wine, where travelers plunder clusters of dates, where langurs lick the sweet-smelling molasses-juice, [trees] scratched by the beaks of <s>cakora</s> birds; whose forest-clearings are never barren, with wilderness-reservoirs surrounded by rows of tall <s>arjuna</s> trees, their banks muddied by cattle descending to drink — sheltering hundreds of travelers, like dams of the forest-<s>Varuṇa</s> (rain-god); crowded with camels and sheep tended by young camel-herder boys; scattered in every direction with herds of mares roaming freely like wind-deer, facing upward with flared nostrils as if drinking the wind to quicken the foals sleeping in their bellies, their rolling-grounds' crushed <s>kuṅkuma</s>-earth stained as if to entice the horses of the sun-chariot; whose world is whitened by virtues like flocks of swans appearing in the smoke-darkness of unceasing sacrificial fires; whose populace is made vocal by splendors like peacocks maddened by the drum-sounds accompanying musical performances; adorned by worthy men like pearls, round and white as moonbeams; approachable by—

children.text: -gamanīyaḥ, mṛga-mada-parimala-vāhi-mṛga-româcchāditair himavat-pādair iva mahattaraiḥ sthirī-kṛtaḥ, proddaṇḍa-sahasra-patrôpaviṣṭa-dvijôttamair Nārāyaṇanâbhimaṇḍalair iva toyâśayair maṇḍitaḥ, mathita-payaḥ-pravāha-prakṣālita-kṣitibhiḥ kṣīrôda-mathanârambhair iva mahā-ghoṣaiḥ pūritâśaḥ Śrīkaṇṭho nāma jana-padaḥ.
children.translated_text: —all [as guests] like great trees whose abundant fruits are plucked by hundreds of travelers; made firm by its elders, like the foot-hills of the <s>Himālaya</s>, covered with deer-hide bearing the fragrance of musk; adorned by reservoirs — like the circles of <s>Nārāyaṇa's</s> navel-[lotus] — on whose erect thousand-petaled [lotuses] sit the finest twice-born [birds/Brahmins]; whose horizons are filled by great cattle-stations — like the beginnings of the churning of the Milk-Ocean — washing the earth with streams of churned milk — [such is] the country named <s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s>.

body.translated_text: 'Listen: There is — like the abode of <s>Vāsava</s> (Indra) descended to earth, a dwelling-place of the meritorious — ever undisturbed in the conduct of the [four] <s>varṇas</s>, an establishment of the <s>Kṛtayuga</s> (Golden Age); whose fields are furrowed by ploughs clamorous with bees as though singing the praises of the earth's essential virtue, their clods uprooted by the plough-shares because of the abundance of land-lotuses; unbroken with continuous rows of sugarcane plantations as if watered by clouds drinking the waters of the Milk-Ocean; with heaps of grain dividing all its boundaries into narrow [passages], like unprecedented mountains in every direction — the grain-heaps in threshing-floor storehouses; with soil matted by cumin-tufts being watered on all sides by upraised water-wheels; adorned by the finest <s>śāli</s> rice of its most fertile fields; established upon upland surfaces with stores of wheat turned tawny by burst mung-bean pod-casings and reddened by clusters of ripe kidney-beans; whose forests are whitened by cattle satisfied with easily-cropped grass, tended by singing cowherds seated on buffalo-backs, followed by flocks of sparrows greedy for masses of insects, charming with the clatter of bells fastened in neck-troughs, wandering through the wilderness, giving forth milk in many streams like the Milk-Ocean — as if fearing disease [caused by <s>Hara's</s> bull drinking it] — divided into many parts, dripping with—

body.text: yatra tretâgni-dhūmâśru-pāta-jala-kṣālitā ivâkṣīyanta ku-dṛṣṭayaḥ. pacyamāna-cayanêṣṭakā-dahana-dagdhānîva nâdṛśyanta duritāni. chidyamāna-yūpa-dāru-paraśu-pāṭita iva vyadīryatâdharmaḥ. makha-śikhi-dhūma-jala-dhara-dhārā-dhauta iva nanāśa varṇa-saṃkaraḥ. dīyamānân-eka-go-sahasra-śṛṅga-khaṇḍyamāna ivâpalāyata kaliḥ. surâlaya-śilā-ghaṭṭana-ṭaṅka-nikara-nikṛtā iva vyadīryanta vipadaḥ. mahā-dāna-vidhāna-kalakalâbhidrutā iva prādravann upadravāḥ. dīpyamāna-satra-mahānasa-sahasrânalasaṃtāpitā iva vyalīyanta vyādhayaḥ. vṛṣa-vivāha-prahata-puṇya-paṭaha-paṭu-rava-trāsitā iva nôpāsarpann apamṛtyavaḥ. saṃtata-brahma-ghoṣa-badhirī-kṛtā ivâpajagmur ītayaḥ. dharmâdhikāra-paribhūtam iva na prābhavad dur-vaivam.

children.text: iva bhuvanasya, kuṅkuma-malana-piñjarita-bahu-mahiṣī-sahasra-śobhito 'ntaḥ-pura-niveśa iva dharmasya, marud-uddhūyamāna-camarī-bāla-vyajana-śata-dhavalita-prānta eka-deśa iva sura-rājyasya, jvalan-makha-śikhi-sahasra-dīpyamāna-daśa-dig-antaḥ śibira-saṃniveśa iva kṛta-yugasya; padmâsana-sthita-brahma-rṣi-dhyānâdhīyamāna-sakalâkuśala-praśamaḥ prathamo 'vatāra iva brahma-lokasya, kalakala-mukhara-mahā-vāhinī-śata-saṃkulo vipakṣa ivôttara-Kurūṇām, īśvara-mārgaṇa-saṃtāpân-abhijña-sakala-jano vijigīṣur iva tri-purasya, sudhā-rasa-sikta-dhavala-gṛha-paṅkti-pāṇḍuraḥ pratinidhir iva candra-lokasya, madhu-mada-matta-kāśinī-bhūṣaṇa-rava-bharita-bhuvano nāmâbhihāra iva kubera-nagarasya, sthāṇv-īśvarâkhyo jana-pada-viśeṣaḥ.
children.translated_text: of the world; adorned within by the splendor of thousands of chief queens yellowed by <s>kuṅkuma</s>-paste — like the inner quarters of <s>Dharma</s> [personified]; whitened at the edges by hundreds of waving <s>camarī</s>-tail fans blown by the wind — like a portion of the kingdom of the gods; with all ten directions blazing with thousands of flaming sacrificial fires — like the camp of the <s>Kṛtayuga</s>; whose complete quelling of all misfortune was as if studied through meditation by Brahma-sages seated in lotus-posture — a first descent of the <s>Brahma</s>-world; teeming with hundreds of great armies clamorous with tumult — an opposite of the Northern <s>Kurus</s>; whose entire populace was unacquainted with the anguish of seeking the Lord — a conqueror of the Triple City; white with rows of whitewashed houses sprinkled with lime-juice — a replica of the lunar world; whose world was filled with the sound of ornaments of women of <s>Kāśī</s> intoxicated with the madness of wine — a namesake of <s>Kubera's</s> city — [there was] a particular region called <s>Sthāṇvīśvara</s>.

body.translated_text: Where evil views perished as if washed away by tear-drops of the smoke of the three sacrificial fires; where sins were unseen as if burnt by the fire baking the bricks for the sacrificial altar; where <s>adharma</s> was split asunder as if cut by the axe chopping the sacrificial post-wood; where mixture of <s>varṇas</s> was destroyed as if washed by the rain-cloud streams of sacrificial fire-smoke; where the <s>Kali</s> age fled as if its horn was being broken by the thousands of cow-gifts being given; where calamities were shattered as if cut by the multitude of chisels striking the stone of god-temples; where disasters fled as if chased by the tumult of the arrangement of great gifts; where diseases vanished as if scorched by the thousands of fires in the great kitchens of burning <s>satras</s> (sacrificial sessions); where untimely deaths did not approach as if frightened by the loud beat of auspicious drums at bull-weddings; where afflictions departed as if deafened by continuous <s>Vedic</s> chanting; where ill-fate did not prevail as if subdued by the authority of <s>dharma</s>.

children.translated_text: —ascetics as a <s>Śākya</s> hermitage, by lovers as a city of <s>Apsarases</s>, by performers as a great festival assembly, and by Brahmins as a stream of wealth.

body.translated_text: Which was apprehended by sages as a forest of penance, by courtesans as a temple of desire, by dancers as a music-hall, by enemies as the city of <s>Yama</s>, by supplicants as the land of the wish-fulfilling gem, by those living by arms as a field of heroes, by students as a teacher's establishment, by singers as a city of <s>Gandharvas</s>, by scientists as the workshop of <s>Viśvakarman</s>, by merchants as a land of profit, by bards as a gambling-house, by the virtuous as an assembly of the good, by refugees as a cage of adamant, by connoisseurs as a gathering of gallants, by travelers as the fruit of merit, by eccentrics as a cave of <s>Asuras</s>, by—

body.text: yatra ca mātaṅga-gāminyaḥ śīlavatyaś ca, gauryo vibhava-ratāś ca, śmāmāḥ padma-rāgiṇyaś ca, dhavala-dvija-śuci-vadanā madirâmodi-śvasanāś ca, candra-kānta-vapuṣaḥ śirīṣa-komalâṅgyaś ca, a-bhujaṅga-gamyāḥ kañcukinyaś ca, pṛthu-kalatra-śriyo daridra-madhya-kalitāś ca, lāvaṇyavatyo madhura-bhāṣiṇyaś ca, a-pramattāḥ prasannôjjvala-mukha-rāgāś ca a-kautukāḥ prauḍhāś ca pramadāḥ.
body.translated_text: And where the women were: of elephant-gait yet virtuous; fair-complexioned yet delighting in riches; dark yet passionate for lotuses; white-toothed and pure-faced yet with breath fragrant of wine; moon-bright in body yet delicate of limb like the <s>śirīṣa</s> flower; inaccessible to [deceitful] serpents yet wearing bodices; of broad hip-splendor yet slender-waisted; possessing charm yet sweet-spoken; vigilant yet with clear, radiant face-color; unadorned yet mature — [such were] the beautiful women.

body.text: yatra ca pramadānāṃ cakṣur eva sahajaṃ muṇḍa-mālā-maṇḍanaṃ bhāraḥ kuvalaya-dala-dāmāni, alaka-pratibimbāny eva kapola-tala-gatāny a-kliṣṭāḥ śravaṇâvataṃsāḥ punar-uktāni tamāla-kisalayāni, priya-kathā eva subhagāḥ karṇâlaṃkārā āḍambaraḥ kumḍalâdiḥ, kapolā eva satatam āloka-kārakā vibhavo niḥśvāsa-maṇi-pradopāḥ surabhi-niḥsvāsâkṛṣṭaṃ madhu-kara-kulam eva ramaṇīyaṃ mukhâvaraṇaṃ kula-strī-janâcāro jālikā, vāṇy eva madhuratarā vīṇā bāhya-vijñānaṃ tantrī-tāḍanam, hāsā evâti-

children.text: -śaya-surabhayaḥ paṭa-vāsā nir-arthakāḥ karpūra-pāṃsavaḥ, adhara-kānti-visara evôjjvalataro 'ṅga-rāgo nir-guṇo lāvaṇya-kalaṅkaḥ kuṅkuma-paṅkaḥ, bāhava eva komalatamāḥ, parihāsa-prahāra-vetra-latā niṣ-prayojanāni mṛṇālāni, yauvanôṣma-sveda-bindava eva vidagdhāḥ kucâlaṃ-kṛtayo hārās tu bhārāḥ, śroṇya eva viśāla-sphaṭika-śilātala-caturasrā rāgiṇāṃ viśrama-kāraṇam a-nimittaṃ bhavana-maṇi-vedikāḥ. kamala-lobha-nilānāny ali-kulāny eva mukharāṇi padâbharaṇakāni niṣ-phalānîndra-nīla-maṇi-nūpurāṇi. nūpura-ravâhṛtā bhavana-kalahaṃsā eva samucitāḥ saṃcaraṇa-sahāyā aiśvarya-prapañcāḥ parijanāḥ.
children.translated_text: —fragrant — cloth-perfumes and camphor-powder being pointless; the radiance of their lips alone was the more brilliant body-paint — <s>kuṅkuma</s> paste being a blemish upon [natural] beauty with no merit; their arms alone were the softest — playful-blow creeper-switches and lotus-stems being purposeless; the sweat-drops of youthful heat alone were the expert breast-ornaments — pearl-necklaces being [mere] burdens; their hips alone were the broad, flat crystal-surfaces — the resting-place of the passionate, the gem-platforms of their mansions being without cause; bee-swarms blue from lotus-greed alone were the melodious foot-ornaments — sapphire anklets being fruitless; house-geese attracted by ankle-bell sounds alone were the proper walking-companions — retinues of servants being elaborate displays of sovereignty.

body.translated_text: And where, for the beautiful women: their eyes alone were the natural adornment of skull-garlands — [actual] <s>kuvalaya</s>-petal wreaths being [mere] burdens; the reflections of curls on their cheek-surfaces alone were the effortless ear-ornaments — <s>tamāla</s> shoots being redundant; their beloved's words alone were the charming ear-decorations — earrings and such being ostentation; their cheeks alone were the perpetual illuminators — jeweled lamps of sighs being [superfluous] splendor; the cluster of bees drawn by fragrant breath alone was the lovely face-veil — the lattice-screen being [mere] family-woman's custom; their speech alone was the sweeter <s>vīṇā</s> — plucking of strings being external artifice; their laughter alone was supremely—

body.translated_text: And there — like <s>Sahasrākṣa</s> (Thousand-eyed Indra) himself, bearing a bow of all colors; like one made of <s>Meru</s> in [the matter of] auspicious nature; like one made of <s>Mandara</s> in attracting <s>Lakṣmī</s> (prosperity); like one made of the Ocean in propriety; like one made of Space in the manifestation of fame; like one made of the Moon in the collection of arts; like one made of the <s>Vedas</s> in natural, unaffected speech; like one made of the Earth in sustaining the world; like one made of Wind in removing the dust-impurities of all earthly [kings]; weighty like <s>Guru</s> (<s>Bṛhaspati</s>) in speech; broad like <s>Pṛthu</s> in chest; expansive like <s>Viśāla</s> in mind; like <s>Janaka</s> in austerity; like <s>Suyātra</s> in brilliance; like <s>Sumantra</s> in counsel; like <s>Budha</s> (Mercury) in assembly; like <s>Arjuna</s> in fame; like <s>Bhīṣma</s> in archery; like <s>Niṣadha</s> [Nala] in—

body.text: Pṛthunā gaur ivêyaṃ kṛtêti yaḥ spardhamāna iva mahīṃ mahiṣīṃ cakāra. nisarga-svairiṇī sva-rucy-anurodhinī ca bhavati hi mahatāṃ matiḥ. yatas tasya kena-cid an-upadiṣṭā sahajâiva śaiśavād ārabhyân-anya-devatā bhagavati, bhakti-sulabhe, bhuvana-bhṛti, bhūta-bhāvane, bhava-cchidi, bhave bhūyasī bhaktir abhūt. a-kṛta-vṛṣabha-dhvaja-pūjā-vidhir na svapne 'py āhāram akarot. a-jam, a-jaram, a-mara-gurum, asura-pura-ripum, a-parimita-gaṇa-patim, a-cala-duhitṛ-patim, akhila-bhuvana-kṛta-caraṇa-natim, paśu-patiṃ prapanno 'nya-devatā-śūnyam amanyata trailokyam. bhartṛ-cittânuvartinyaś cânujīvināṃ prakṛtayaḥ. tathā hi: gṛhe gṛhe bhagavān apūjyata khaṇḍa-paraśuḥ. vavur asya homâlavālânala-vilīyamāna-bahala-guggulu-gandha-garbhāḥ snapana-kṣīra-śīkara-kṣoda-kṣāriṇo bilva-pallava-dāma-dalôdvāhinaḥ puṇya-viṣayeṣu vāyavaḥ. Śiva-saparyā-samucitair upāyanaiḥ prābhṛtaiś ca paurāḥ pādôpajīvinaḥ sacivāḥ sva-bhuja-bala-nirjitāś ca karadī-kṛtā mahā-sāmantās taṃ siṣevire. tathā hi: Kailāsa-kūṭa-dhavalaiḥ kanaka-patra-latâlaṅ-kṛta-viṣāṇa-koṭibhir mahā-pramāṇaiḥ saṃdhyā-bali-vṛṣaiḥ sauvarṇaiś ca snapana-kalaśair argha-bhājanaiś ca dhūpa-pātraiś ca puṣpa-paṭṭaiś ca maṇi-yaṣṭi-pradīpaiś ca brahma-sūtraiś ca mahârha-māṇikya-khaṇḍa-khacitaiś ca mukha-koṣaiḥ paritoṣam asya manasi cakruḥ. antaḥ-purāṇy api svayam-ārabdha-bāleya-taṇḍula-kaṇḍanāni deva-gṛhôpalepana-lohitatara-kara-kisalayāni kusuma-grathana-vyagra-samasta-parijanāni tasyâbhilaṣitam anvavartanta. tathā ca parama-māheśvaraḥ sa bhū-pālo lokataḥ

children.text: śuśrāva bhuvi bhagavantam a-param iva sākṣād dakṣa-makha-mathanaṃ dākṣiṇātyaṃ bahu-vidha-vidyā-prabhāva-prakhyātair guṇaiḥ śiṣyair ivân-eka-sahasra-saṃkhyair vyāpta-martya-lokaṃ Bhairavācārya-nāmānaṃ mahā-śaivam. upanayanti hi hṛdayam a-dṛṣṭam api janaṃ śīla-saṃvādāḥ. yataḥ sa rājā śravaṇa-sama-kālam eva tasmin Bhairavācārye bhagavati dvitīya iva kapardini dūra-gate 'pi garīyasīṃ babandha bhaktim. ācakāṅkṣa ca mano-rathair apy asya sarvathā darśanam.
children.translated_text: heard that on earth there was a great <s>Śaiva</s> master named <s>Bhairavācārya</s>, from the south, who was like a second destroyer of <s>Dakṣa</s>'s sacrifice in person, whose disciples—numbering in many thousands, renowned for the power of manifold arts—had pervaded the mortal world. For affinities of character draw the heart even toward a person one has never seen. Therefore, the king, at the very moment of hearing, developed great devotion toward that <s>Bhairavācārya</s>, as if toward a second <s>Kapardī</s> (Śiva with matted locks), though he was far away. And he longed by all means to see him, even if only in his imaginings.

body.translated_text: As if rivaling <s>Pṛthu</s>, who made the earth into a cow, he made the earth his queen. For the mind of great men is by nature independent and follows its own inclination. Therefore, untaught by anyone, innately from childhood itself, he developed supreme devotion to Lord <s>Bhava</s> (Śiva)—who is accessible through devotion, who sustains the worlds, who nurtures all beings, and who destroys the bonds of worldly existence—acknowledging no other deity. Without having performed the worship of Him whose banner bears the bull, he would not take food even in his dreams. Having taken refuge in <s>Paśupati</s>—the unborn, the ageless, the teacher of the immortals, the enemy of demon-cities, the lord of innumerable <s>gaṇas</s>, the husband of the mountain's daughter, at whose feet the entire universe bows—he considered the three worlds devoid of any other deity. And the dispositions of dependents follow the mind of their master. Thus, in every house the Lord of the broken axe was worshipped. Winds blew in his domains, bearing the fragrance of thick <s>guggulu</s> incense dissolving in the fires of sacrificial pits, moistened with drops of bathing milk, carrying garlands of <s>bilva</s> leaves—auspicious winds. The citizens, the servants at his feet, the ministers, and the great feudatories subdued by the might of his arms and made tributary, all served him with gifts and offerings befitting the worship of <s>Śiva</s>. Thus, they delighted his heart with bulls for the twilight offering—white as the peaks of <s>Kailāsa</s>, with horn-tips adorned with golden leaf-creepers, of great size—with golden bathing vessels, offering bowls, incense holders, flower-cloths, jeweled lamp-stands, sacred threads, and face-covers studded with precious rubies. Even the queens of the inner apartments followed his wishes, with their own hands pounding young rice grains, their tender hand-shoots reddened from plastering the temple floors, all their attendants busy stringing flowers. And thus that king, the supreme devotee of <s>Maheśvara</s>, from the people
